title: Ang 1429: the seal
hook: the Mundavani's plate of truth, contentment and reflection, and a closing salok of thanks
tomorrow: so what's left on the very last page?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the ninth Guru's saloks: everything you see passes, and the Name remains. One page before the hymns close.

A wax seal on a letter used to say two things: it's finished, and here's whose it is. The Granth has one. It's near the end of a full reading. The room is packed, the karah prashad sits covered by the platform, and the reader turns to ang 1429. Kids who fidgeted for an hour go still. The last hymn before the seal isn't a rule or a warning. It's about a plate. Three things are on it, and then one more. What are they?
screen: `A SEAL: FINISHED, AND WHOSE.` → `A PACKED ROOM, ANG 1429.` → `A PLATE. WHAT'S ON IT?`

segments.voice: Guru Arjan wrote it, and its name, Mundavani, is usually rendered as the seal. In paraphrase: on this plate three things are placed, truth, contentment and reflection. The Name of the Lord, the nectar that holds everyone up, is placed there too. Whoever eats it, whoever savors it, is saved. This can't be given up; keep it in your heart, always. The dark world is crossed by holding to the Lord's feet, and, Nanak, all of it is the Lord's own spread. So the hymns of the Granth end the way a family meal ends: with a plate passed around. Not a recap of everything before it. Something to eat. And look at what's on it. Truth, contentment, reflection: none of them can be bought, and all of them go slowly. Then comes a salok, also Guru Arjan's, and it's pure thanks. In paraphrase: I didn't recognize what you'd done for me; you made me worthy. I had no virtue; you took pity on me yourself. Mercy came, and I met the True Guru, my friend. Nanak says: if I receive the Name, I live, and body and mind turn green. That's the other side of the seal. The book doesn't close on a lecture. It closes on a gift, and on gratitude for the gift.
screen: `MUNDAVANI: THE SEAL.` · `TRUTH, CONTENTMENT, REFLECTION.` · `A PLATE, NOT A RECAP.` · `THEN A SALOK OF THANKS.` · then, large: `THE SEAL.`

segments.voice: Read ang 1429 if it's near you. Or say the plate out loud, slowly: truth, contentment, reflection, the Name. Pause after each one, as if setting a bowl down on the table, and let the sit hold all four.
Ang 1429. Guru Arjan's Mundavani, a plate of truth, contentment and reflection with the Name, then a salok of thanks.
Your line: the seal. A plate set on the table, and thanks said over it. One page left.

howItsDone: When Sikhs complete a full reading of the Guru Granth Sahib, the Mundavani and the salok of thanks on ang 1429 come near the end, and the reading closes with Anand Sahib, Ardas and karah prashad shared with everyone present.
